newsitem.title: ALBANIA: OSCE vote monitors begin Albania deployment.
newsitem.headline: OSCE vote monitors begin Albania deployment.

text.p: An advance team of OSCE monitors who will oversee Albania's special elections on June 29 began work on Tuesday with security escorts from the multinational force.

"This morning we are deploying a team, some people for the start of our mission," Patrick Keogh, logistics officer for the election mission from the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), told Reuters Television.
"We are deploying 28 people this morning in cars to the outlying surrounding districts of Tirana," Keogh said, adding that teams would go to Durres, Elbasan, Kavaje and Kruje.
"We are not expecting any trouble on the route," Keogh said. "The people we are deploying are technical experts who will go to different areas to assess the situation."
The teams left a downtown Tirana hotel in local taxis hired by the OSCE and emblazoned with OSCE stickers.

They were escorted by jeeps of Italian, Greek and Turkish troops from the multinational force sent to Albania following riots that erupted in March after the collapse of dubious pyramid investment schemes wiped out the savings of thousands of people.

Albanian political parties agreed earlier this month to hold early parliamentary elections as part of an effort to defuse the crisis which threatened to plunge the Balkan nation of 3.4 million people into chaos.
